about: what a first boot of ermineOS puts on the SD card (c/host.c): nodes, each at its parent's names, with a value or a program's source; and what boots, in order, each started as its actor

nodes.name: text
nodes.value:
a workspace: text kept in the graph, at /apps/workspace/text.

cmd-s saves it. Open any node in an editor from the graph browser (alt-g, then enter),
or from a shell: edit /programs/status.

nodes.name: Welcome
nodes.value:
Welcome to your computer.

This is your home, /home. What you keep here stays on this
machine's card, and goes wherever you share it.

  Notes      for writing things down; cmd-n makes a new note
  Pictures   a few to start with: open one, then Set as Desktop
  Trash      what you throw away waits here until you empty it

Double-click to open. The arrow at the top left goes up a
folder; the path at the bottom goes anywhere, as far as /, the
whole graph. Every folder here is a node, and so is every file:
a node can hold a value and other nodes at once.

Connect... mounts a node someone shared with you: paste the id
their share printed, give it a name, and it shows up here, live.

Have a lovely day.

nodes.name: Things to try
nodes.value:
Things to try

- write a note and save it with cmd-s
- make a folder for a project
- set the gingham as your desktop
- open / and wander about: everything on this machine is a node
